observation.visible_scene: A human skull (appearing dark, charred or shadowed) is held in a fixed, centered position against a pure black background. Orange-yellow flames burn around it: a steady flame at the lower jaw/teeth region, a steady flame curving up the right side of the skull, and intermittent flames at the top of the cranium and inside the nasal cavity.
visible_changes: The skull itself does not move; its position and orientation are identical in the first and last frames, and the black background shows no shift, so there is no camera pan/zoom and no object translation.
The lower-jaw flame persists across the whole excerpt but continuously changes shape and height (flickering), never vanishing.
The right-side flame also persists throughout, its curve and vertical extent varying from frame to frame.

The top-of-cranium flame flickers: it grows tall around t=0.25-0.33 and t=0.75-0.92 and again near t=1.33-1.58, then shrinks to a thin tongue or disappears entirely (e.g. absent around t=1.67-2.0 and in several later frames), i.e. an expansion/contraction of flame extent, not a moving object.
The small flame in the nasal cavity repeatedly appears, curls, and fades out (visible strongly at t=0.08-0.58 and t=0.83-1.0, faint or gone at other times).
All visible motion is the unsteady, dancing deformation of the flames; no part of the skull is seen to move, fall, or be displaced.
outside_clip_unknowns: What ignited the flames or what fuel is burning is not shown.
Whether the skull is being consumed or merely surrounded by fire, and the outcome after t=3.33, are outside the excerpt.
The state before t=0 (whether flames were already at these intensities) is unknown; the fire is already ongoing at the first frame.
uncertain_details: The skull's material (bone, prop, or charred surface) cannot be confirmed from the dark lighting.
Whether the top and nasal flames originate from the same source as the lower/right flames or from separate points is not determinable.
Any very slight camera drift is unsupported; background evidence is insufficient to confirm or deny it, so the skull is treated as stationary.

NOT match or connect as a loop. Do not judge different endpoints as a physical inconsistency,
and do not invent a trigger, contact, start, stop, landing, disappearance or completion to make
the excerpt form a complete story. Missing context outside this segment stays unknown.
If an editing cut is visible inside the segment, distinguish it from continuous physical motion;
do not invent a smooth transition or a causal mechanism to connect the two views.
Describe what is visible during the excerpt, the actual changes, and supported persistent
properties. Cover the main visible process, not just scenery. Distinguish object movement from
camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from
occlusion, and an already ongoing process from its onset. Only state what the clip supports;
do not invent causes, an earlier impact, an unseen operator, material identities or later outcomes.
Do not infer motion from one frame, a visible seam or a single pose. Static intervals are valid.
Do not supply named physics laws. Compare each important entity's first and last image positions
and their relative positions before describing motion. Treat camera motion as uncertain when the
background evidence is insufficient, and retain clear relative changes despite that uncertainty.
